topicName: Binary Trees: Properties, Traversal (Inorder, Preorder, Postorder)
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Binary Trees: Properties and Traversal"},{"order":2,"type":"subheading","text":"Introduction to Binary Trees"},{"order":3,"type":"paragraph","text":"A binary tree is a hierarchical data structure in which each node has at most two children, referred to as the left child and the right child. Binary trees are widely used in computer science for various applications, including searching, sorting, and data representation."},{"order":4,"type":"subheading","text":"Properties of Binary Trees"},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Root: The topmost node in the tree."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Child: A node directly connected to another node when moving away from the root."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Parent: The converse notion of a child."},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Siblings: Nodes that share the same parent."},{"order":9,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Leaf: A node with no children."},{"order":10,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Edge: The connection between one node and another."},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Path: A sequence of nodes and edges connecting a node to a descendant."},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Height: The number of edges on the longest path between a node and a descendant leaf."},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Depth: The number of edges from the root to the node."},{"order":14,"type":"subheading","text":"Types of Binary Trees"},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Full Binary Tree: Every node has either 0 or 2 children."},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Complete Binary Tree: All levels are completely filled except possibly the last level and the last level has all keys as left as possible."},{"order":17,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Perfect Binary Tree: All internal nodes have two children and all leaves are at the same level."},{"order":18,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Balanced Binary Tree: The height of the left and right subtrees of every node differ by at most 1."},{"order":19,"type":"subheading","text":"Binary Tree Traversal"},{"order":20,"type":"paragraph","text":"Binary tree traversal refers to the process of visiting each node in the tree exactly once. There are two main types of traversal: depth-first traversal and breadth-first traversal. Depth-first traversal explores as far as possible along each branch before backtracking. Breadth-first traversal visits all the nodes at the same level before moving to the next level."},{"order":21,"type":"subheading","text":"Depth-First Traversal"},{"order":22,"type":"paragraph","text":"Depth-first traversal can be further categorized into three types:"},{"order":23,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Inorder Traversal (Left, Root, Right)"},{"order":24,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Preorder Traversal (Root, Left, Right)"},{"order":25,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Postorder Traversal (Left, Right, Root)"},{"order":26,"type":"subheading","text":"Inorder Traversal"},{"order":27,"type":"paragraph","text":"Inorder traversal visits the left subtree, then the root, and finally the right subtree. This is commonly used to traverse a binary search tree in sorted order."},{"order":28,"type":"code","text":"def inorder_traversal(root):
  if root:
    inorder_traversal(root.left)
    print(root.data, end=' ')
    inorder_traversal(root.right)"},{"order":29,"type":"subheading","text":"Preorder Traversal"},{"order":30,"type":"paragraph","text":"Preorder traversal visits the root, then the left subtree, and finally the right subtree. This is often used to create a prefix expression from an expression tree."},{"order":31,"type":"code","text":"def preorder_traversal(root):
  if root:
    print(root.data, end=' ')
    preorder_traversal(root.left)
    preorder_traversal(root.right)"},{"order":32,"type":"subheading","text":"Postorder Traversal"},{"order":33,"type":"paragraph","text":"Postorder traversal visits the left subtree, then the right subtree, and finally the root. This is commonly used to delete a tree or to create a postfix expression from an expression tree."},{"order":34,"type":"code","text":"def postorder_traversal(root):
  if root:
    postorder_traversal(root.left)
    postorder_traversal(root.right)
    print(root.data, end=' ')"},{"order":35,"type":"subheading","text":"Example"},{"order":36,"type":"paragraph","text":"Consider a binary tree with the following structure:"},{"order":37,"type":"paragraph","text":"      1
     / \
    2   3
   / \
  4   5"},{"order":38,"type":"paragraph","text":"Inorder traversal: 4 2 5 1 3"},{"order":39,"type":"paragraph","text":"Preorder traversal: 1 2 4 5 3"},{"order":40,"type":"paragraph","text":"Postorder traversal: 4 5 2 3 1"}]
